items.title: Unify session identity across REST, WebSocket and /intel (one session model)
follow_ups: Tier: P0. Evidence: REST uses uuid sessions + InMemorySessionStore; ws.py and /intel/sessions/{run_id}/snapshot use int run_id via SessionService, whose repo calls silently no-op against InMemorySessionStore (snapshot always empty, WS entries never persisted). /api/v1/stream duplicates ws.py. GameService is built but referenced by no router.
Scope: one id type, one store API, one WS endpoint; decide fate of SessionService, GameService and the duplicate in-memory repos.
Depends on: REQ-0003. ADR likely: yes (cross-cutting convention, two viable approaches).

Architecture review: ADR-0002 (docs/adr/0002-single-session-model.md, status proposed) chose Option A: delete SessionService and GameService, keep app/services/repos.py InMemorySessionStore as the single store, port ws.py and /intel snapshot to uuid session ids via the SessionStore Protocol, remove /api/v1/stream, add shared message-submit helper. data/repos.py deferred to REQ-0005; REQ-0012 may delete it only after REQ-0005. Pattern PAT-ARCH-001 proposed.

Spec drafted (6 work packages, WP-1 helper first; WP-5 deletions after WP-3/WP-4). Awaiting human acceptance of ADR-0002 and PAT-ARCH-001 (both proposed) before implementation. Open question for human: dropping WS 'token' event and in-WS 'cancel' until REQ-0007.
inference_service worker sets status=error before writing meta.error; swap the two calls so a WS poll cannot see error without its text (candidate for REQ-0007)

inference_service.enqueue writes status=queued after put_nowait; a fast worker terminal status could be overwritten, leaving the WS waiting until the reply timeout; set queued before put_nowait (candidate for REQ-0007)
ws.py: no prompt length limit on WS (REST has 4096-char cap) (candidate for REQ-0010). Non-JSON frames are now handled (error event, socket stays open) - fixed 2026-10-11.

cleanup candidates for REQ-0012: duplicate router= line in session.py, stale docstring in data/repos.py ("Used by GameService"), repos.py docstring refers to app.types, keys.txt/all_files.txt/corpus.txt are stale snapshots naming removed modules and are tracked

items.title: Real, non-blocking streaming and honest inference health
follow_ups: Tier: P1, needed by the frontend. Evidence: generate_tokens calls sync httpx inside an async generator (blocks the event loop) and emits one 'token'; settings.ollama.stream is unused; the WS path bypasses the FIFO queue so REST and WS can hit Ollama concurrently; cancel cannot stop a running job; model_loaded is hard-coded True.
Scope: Ollama NDJSON streaming via httpx.AsyncClient, one serialized path for REST and WS, cancel mid-stream, real health probe, and a documented WS event protocol (token/done/error/status).
Depends on: REQ-0004, REQ-0006. ADR likely: yes (streaming protocol is a cross-cutting contract with the frontend).
Re-scoped 2026-11-01 as 'The DM talks' (slice 2 of the north star; see REQ-0020 follow-ups). Independent of REQ-0020 and REQ-0021.
Central design question: worker thread to WebSocket token path, either an in-memory channel or incremental store writes.
Missing artifact: no WS contract doc exists (docs/api/ does not exist); the token, done and cancel events must be documented in the spec.
Cancellation mid-stream is in scope. ADR expected.

Size sketch: client stream method M; worker token channel M; WS token, done and cancel events M; frontend token accumulation S; WS contract doc S. Rough LOC: backend 200-300, frontend 80-120, tests 110-150.

2026-11-07 priorities assessment (owner-approved): DEFERRED. Owner says local-compute latency (RTX 3070) is acceptable; stream is hard-coded False in app/intelligence/client.py and the WebSocket 'stream' emits one chunk after the whole reply. Revisit if long replies hurt play.

Sequencing: ships before REQ-0028 so the approval queue never mines non-canon messages.

GAP (blocks COMPLETE): a queue-full regenerate (429) calls enqueue, which sets the user message to status error before returning. The user turn then drops out of the prompt history while its completed reply stays in, leaving an orphan reply. Fix: check queue capacity before writing status, or restore the prior status on rejection; add a test asserting the user status is unchanged after a 429 regenerate (tests/test_message_corrections_api.py, tests/test_ws_session.py).
(1) frontend Save closes the editor before the PATCH result, so typed text is lost on failure (NarrativeLog/App).
(2) the regenerate REST route and post_message lack a response_model (PAT-ARCH-005).

(3) update_message merges meta over old meta, so keys a regenerated tool reply omits persist; includes the stale meta.error left on the user message after a failed regenerate is retried (no test asserts it is cleared).
(4) no pytest-timeout or bounded WS receive helper, so a red WS test hangs.
(5) no WS API doc exists for the regenerate action.
(6) frontend has no JS test runner: UI behaviour is checked only by build and manual smoke. A manual smoke with Ollama is still owed.
(7) REQ-0028 (mention detection) must honour canon=false when mining messages.
Minor: ws.py sends the user entry snapshotted before enqueue, so it shows status completed while queued (WP-7 asks for the fresh message).
Minor: regenerate check-then-enqueue is not locked, so two concurrent regenerates can both pass the 409 check, running the chat twice and recording two revisions (one reply row is kept).

update_message_status merges meta and cannot delete keys: a rejected regenerate on a message that never had 'error' leaves 'error': null and updated_by behind; a replace-meta store method would clean it up. Also enqueue sets 'queued' before put_nowait, so a non-Full exception leaves the status queued (regenerate now restores, root cause is in enqueue).
